name: Hsu Shou-Hsiung
forbes_bio: Hsu Shou-Hsiung is vice chairman of Fortune Electric, a maker of transformers, switchboards and other heavy electrical equipment.
It was founded by Shou-Hsiung's late father, Hsu Hsien-Liang, in 1969, and listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 1997.
Shou-Hsiung's son I-Sheng serves as Fortune Electric's CEO.
In 2025, the company won a NT$2 billion ($68 million) transformer order for the Stargate project, a $500 billion AI infrastructure project led by companies such as SoftBank, OpenAI and Oracle.

name: Gao Jinzhu
forbes_bio: Gao Jinzhu is the executive director of Wanguo Gold Group, a China-based mining and processing company.
Gao's son, Wang Renxiang, is executive director of the company.
Gao Mingqing, who works with Gao Jinzhu at the company, is its chairman and also a billionaire.

name: Alan Rydge
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2022); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Alan Rydge is chairman and lead shareholder of cinema, hotel and ski-resort group EVT, formerly Event Hospitality & Entertainment.
He inherited the Greater Union cinema chain after his father died in 1980.
He's also chairman and the major shareholder of investment firm Carlton Investments.

name: Cheng Zhangwen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2014-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Cheng Zhangwen is a director of Neway Valve (Suzhou).
Cheng co-founded the company in 1997 with Wang Baoqing, Lu Bin and Xi Chao.
The company went public in 2014.
The company has subsidiaries in the United States, Dubai, the Netherlands, Italy, Singapore and Nigeria.

name: Delfin Jorge Ezequiel Carballo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Delfín Jorge Ezequiel Carballo cofounded Macro Compañía Financiera in 1978, laying the foundation for what has become Argentina's largest bank, Banco Macro.
The bank went public in Buenos Aires in 1994 and started trading on the New York Stock Exchange in 2006.
Carballo's business partner and Banco Macro cofounder Jorge Brito died in a plane crash in 2020, shortly after resuming his role as chairman following a hiatus due to a corruption scandal.
Carballo, who took over after Brito's passing, stepped down from his chairman role in 2023. Brito's son Jorge Pablo is now at the helm.
forbes_facts: Carballo's sister Marcela is the widow of Jorge Brito.
After acquiring Banco Itau in 2023, Banco Macro now has 567 branches and more than 6 million customers.

name: Leone Benetton
forbes_bio: Leone Benetton is the son of Carlo Benetton (d. 2018), one of the co-founders of the Benetton Group.
Known for their colorful sweaters, Benetton won over parts of the world, opening its first store in Paris in 1969 and reaching New York in 1980.
The family has invested in Italian businesses including Mundys, a highway infrastructure company that accounts for more than half their fortune.
Leone serves as the chairman of Cia de Tierras Sud Argentino, a livestock subsidiary of Edizione Group.

name: Alexander Tedja
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2013-2022); Hurun Global (2018-2025)
forbes_bio: Alexander Tedja's real estate developer Pakuwon Jati was established in 1982 and went public in 1989.
The listed company is known for its mixed-use developments that combine condos, hotels, malls and offices in Jakarta and Surabaya.
In 2022, the company started construction of a 7.2-hectare mixed-use project in Nusantara, the country's upcoming, new capital city.
The company is developing five new hotels, comprising 1,300 rooms across Indonesia, scheduled to open by 2030. They will be operated by Marriott International.
forbes_facts: An art lover, Tedja received the Distinguished Patron of the Arts in 2017 for his long-term loan of a collection of paintings to the National Gallery Singapore.
Tedja's daughter Irene is married to the son of billionaire Murdaya Poo.
Tedja started his career as an executive in the film industry in the 1970s.

name: Linden Blue
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2020); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Linden Blue is a vice chairman at General Atomics, a San Diego-based private company known for its Predator drones.
Blue and his brother Neal bought General Atomics, which pulled in $2.7 billion in sales in 2018, from Chevron in 1986 for a reported $60 million.
The largest private government contractor in the U.S., GA's clients include foreign nations such as Italy, Spain, and the UAE.
Neal Blue, who is the chairman and CEO of the company, is worth $4.1 billion.
forbes_facts: In 1956, Neal, then 21, and Linden, 20, flew across Central and South America on a plane that they piloted. Life Magazine put their excursion on its cover.
After graduating from Yale, the brothers both served in the U.S. Air Force (Neal Blue as a nuclear weapons custodian and Linden Blue as a security police).

name: Rahul Gautam
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2021-2024); Hurun Global (2021-2024); Hurun India (2017-2019)
forbes_bio: Rahul Gautam is the chairman and managing director of Sheela Foam, best known for its Sleepwell brand of mattresses.
The business was set up his late mother Sheela Gautam in 1971.
The company was listed in 2016.
Sheela Foam has 10 factories in India, three in Australia and one in Spain.
In July 2023, Sheela Foam agreed to buy a 95% stake in mattress rival Kurlon Enterprise and a 35% stake in furniture maker Furlenco.
forbes_facts: Gautam's son Tushaar heads research for the company.

name: Niti Osathanugrah
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2024); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Niti Osathanugrah gets a chunk of his wealth from a stake in Osotspa, his family's 133- year-old maker of popular energy drink M-150.
The company got listed in 2018. Niti sits on its board.
Niti also has valuable stakes in fellow billionaire William Heinecke's Minor International as well as Home Product Center, Central Pattana, and CP All.
